stt: Learn Rust by writing a small OS
x:
I recommend Jon Gjengset's book "rust for rustaceans" https://nostarch.com/rust-rustaceans

If you're comfortable in Rust, it is the next step up for intermediate developers.

I like "the book", but I felt more prepared for the real world after reading the O'reilly book, 2nd edition. That was sufficient for me to write any code I needed. If you want a deeper understanding, "Rust for Rustaceans" is a great book (disclaimer: I only read about half of it - too busy coding :-)

First:
https://www.oreilly.com/library/view/programming-rust-2nd/97...

If you want to go deeper after that:
https://nostarch.com/rust-rustaceans

stt: Ask HN: What's the best way to learn Rust in 2022?
x:
The Rust Book is the best introduction I think. Then, Rust for Rustaceans[1] might be the best intermediate to advanced rust book I've ever seen.

Don't forget to practice and work on real projects, the concepts take a little bit to get used to, and just reading about it is not enough.

[1]: https://nostarch.com/rust-rustaceans
